title: Warsh Fed Turns Hawkish as Dot Plot Flips to a Hike and 2026 Cuts Vanish
content: Kevin Warsh's first FOMC as chair on 17 June held policy at 3.50-3.75% but delivered a decisive hawkish regime shift that dominated cross-asset trading through the window. A pared-back 130-word statement, an upgraded SEP and a dot plot that erased 2026 easing, with nine of eighteen members now pencilling in a hike, pushed Fed-funds futures to price roughly 77% odds of a December hike, up from about 24% a month earlier. Sticky inflation reinforced the tilt, with May CPI running near 4.2% y/y, and the July release of the June minutes showed officials split but leaning hawkish. Two-year UST yields and the USD firmed, with USD/JPY pressing 40-year lows near 162 and intervention chatter building. Higher-for-longer weighed on long-duration equities and left rate-sensitive assets hostage to each data print.

title: AI and Semiconductor Leadership Powers Record Highs Before a Late-Window Wobble
content: The mega-cap AI and chip complex remained the engine of the equity advance, capping the strongest quarter since 2020 and lifting the Dow to a record close above 53,000 as Q3 opened. Semiconductor and equipment names contributed almost half of the S&P 500's market-value gains this year, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index up around 75% year-to-date. Yet leadership grew visibly fragile into July: the S&P 500 and Nasdaq slipped roughly 2% and 5% from their 2 June peaks as chipmakers wavered and investors questioned stretched valuations and heavy concentration in a handful of names. Commentators flagged the hottest rally losing steam, debating whether an AI-capex breakout or a correction lay ahead. Higher-for-longer rates compounded the pressure on long-duration multiples, keeping breadth, positioning and any crack in tech sentiment central to the broader tape.

title: Renewed US-Iran Strikes Revive the Oil Risk Premium and Hormuz Supply Fears
content: After a brief return toward pre-war levels, the Middle East risk premium roared back as US-Iran hostilities reignited across the window, reversing the earlier de-escalation. Attacks on vessels in and near the Strait of Hormuz, a US strike on Iran around 8 July, President Trump's threat to blockade Tehran, and the Treasury's revocation of a 60-day sanctions waiver disrupted a fragile recovery in Gulf tanker traffic. Brent pushed back above $76, posting a weekly gain near 6%, while WTI stabilised above $72. Because Hormuz carries roughly a fifth of global oil and gas trade, the renewed threat kept a supply premium embedded in crude even as technical talks continued. The rebound complicated the inflation outlook just as the Fed turned hawkish, pressured oil-dependent importers such as a yen-weakened Japan, supported energy equities and unsettled broader risk sentiment.
